frameworkBasis.firstBoundary: Wrangler cli.js311625-311632 onProxyWorkerMessage(type=error) emits reason Error inside ProxyWorker; cli.js311742-311755 wraps error as ProxyController with cast cause.
frameworkBasis.secondBoundary: Miniflare index.js88260-88278 dispatches custom loopback service(request,this) and reports thrown errors as500.
frameworkBasis.doesNotEstablish: Originating URL/request, external terminator, ordinary observer body cancellation, CPU/OOM, cache/build contention, or automatic-monitor mis-kill

random explicit loopback ports outside3000/5791/5432/555xx; harmless Worker/HTTP fixtures

cases: Baseline healthy fetch and complete consume/discard body
Explicitly stop only the fixture Wrangler parent, and separately only its owned workerd descendant; record intent/PID/creation/exit and compare observed proxy error
Abrupt close/reset of only the fixture proxy/outbound socket without process termination
Consumer cancellation/abort and server disposal as distinct isolated actions, alongside ordinary response completion
Concurrent private build/cache activity in separate versus deliberately shared fixture-only paths; never target actual runtime
If a first failure reproduces, reduce to that boundary before any production repair; keep identity/owned-tree gates and max5/10min rate guard
measurements: Actual native child and descendant PID/creation/argv hash and confirmed exit; no generic name-based termination
Action intent UTC, framework message/error, HTTP outcome and bounded request phase/event correlation
No blanket suppression of ProxyWorker errors or HTTP200 substitution for failure
Lossy/absent trace classified as unknown, not clean/success

limits: Only these selected existing runtime logs/source/receipts were read; no genuine Status/HTTP/SQL/lifecycle/build or heavy reproduction was executed.
No complete OS process-termination audit was supplied. The latest stop file and startup records are observational partial sources, not proof of absence of commands.

If root finds an explicit matching operation, classify it as planned/task-induced or out-of-scope as the real authorization/timing shows; do not keep calling it a proven spontaneous crash.
